editorial:
You follow Elias, a 14-year-old who feels out of place in his quiet village, until Alexander moves in next door and shakes up his world. Their friendship grows fast, but Elias starts noticing feelings he does not fully understand, and that tension gives the movie a soft, honest heartbeat. It feels less like big drama and more like watching two kids learn who they are, with awkward silences, small smiles, and moments that feel painfully real.

The young leads carry the film with natural, understated performances, and the slow pacing lets emotions land without rushing. The village setting adds warmth, though some scenes may feel a little too quiet if you want more action. Still, it is a tender, thoughtful watch for fans of coming-of-age romance.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Elias stops pretending he is fine and finally tells Alexander how he feels. Instead of pushing him away, Alexander listens and accepts him, turning their friendship into something open and real. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with the two boys walking together and Elias no longer feeling trapped by his village or his own fear. There is no shocking twist, just a quiet, emotional release.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves gentle coming-of-age stories and emotional teen romance.
